answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price. Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so I can change vendors this cycle without breach. memory_c2 shows a prior primary switch to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and clean invoicing, which supports a switch_primary_vendor direction. memory_c4 confirms that benchmarking/renegotiation recovers real margin, so the new vendor should be selected with explicit benchmarked pricing rather than a quoted one. memory_c3 demonstrates that a second source removed a single point of failure during a shortage, so I would design the new vendor as a primary swap but introduce the previous incumbent as a qualified second source to control delivery risk while the line is running at 94% with no buffer. Verify c2 to confirm the prior primary switch delivered as remembered (onboarding speed, invoicing accuracy) before committing the line. Verify c3 to confirm the second-source pattern actually protected supply during a shortage before leaning on it here. Limit to one decision this cycle: switch primary to the low-cost vendor with a small guarded test, and qualify the incumbent as second source rather than running two full swaps in parallel.
